Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Formations ● Games 1 (Football, Basketball, Netball, Badminton), part of Coaching 2.4 Tactical skills Athletics ● Track events (sprints, relays hurdles,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 SPORTS AND RECREATION FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why are formations used in sports? 2. How do formation skills enhance performance in games?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Formations ● Games 1 (Football, Basketball, Netball, Badminton) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: the learner manages tasks successfully when demonstrating different formations in selected games.

● Learning to learn: the learner reflects on what they have learnt and adjust accordingly during practice of different formations

in selected games.

● Digital literacy: the learner explores digital spaces when watching videos on training sessions of a coach and critiques the

different formations observed.

Values:
● Respect: the learner understands and appreciates others while watching training sessions of a coach and gives constructive

feedback on the different formations observed.

● Responsibility: the learner proactively solves problems during the practice of different formations of selected games.

● Peace: the learner avoids conflict with others while playing mini games in the selected games to enhance teamwork.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security skills: the learner observes safety in the class and school environment while practising different

formations of selected games.

● Self-management skills: the learner develops self-esteem during demonstration of different formations of selected games.
